contexts.text: If touched with the point of a needle.
The hornets = the dread of those who are in falsities, because they... are furnished with stings, with which they inflict poisoned wounds.
They have stings in their tails () = the cunningnesses of deceiving by means of persuasions. ( = cunning falsifications of the Word. AR 439.)
Points = falsities from evil which hurt. Illustrated.
Thorns, thistles, etc., also = falsities of evil, from their sharp points.
They receive a ring to which brazen points are affixed...

From his eyes... there appeared to go forth rays like bright stings, like those of certain insects which have stings on both sides... He drew back those bright stings, and (projected them in various directions). Explained. SE 3541.
If he approached he would be inwardly lacerated as with thousands of sharp points and of swords...
These are compared to a new threshing instrument furnished with sharp points ().
Stings () = the cunningnesses and craftinesses for the persuading of falsities.

That stings = cunningnesses, is evident... for in common discourse the cunningnesses in speech by which men are deceived are called stings, and the speech itself is called sharp. In special, however, by stings are signified interior falsities, which are such as cannot be shaken off, because they are from the scientifics and fallacies of the senses... In the Spiritual World interior falsities are represented in various ways by sharp things; as by... pointed things in various forms; and this when the intention is to do hurt; and therefore it is forbidden to present such things to view there.
These falsities are signified by stings. Illustrated.
To draw out with stings () = to lead away from truths by scientifics from the Word and the world falsely applied.
For stings in your sides () = that malignant falsities will inflict injury on the goods of the Church.
